newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end easier, second liners wilt.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end easier, second liners wilt.

text.p: Singapore shares ended softer on Friday as investors cut their positions ahead of the weekend.
"There is a bit of uncertainty. The employment data coming out in the U.S. tonight and also Malaysia's DRB/Proton group of companies being traded again next week," said a local broker.
The Malaysian companies were suspended after its chief Yahaya Ahmad died in a helicoptor crash on Monday.
"There could be some weakness which would spill over to the Singapore market, especially the OTC," said the broker.
The Straits Times Industrial Index ended down 1.66 points at 2,178.27 while the UOB-OTC index closed lower at 3.03 1,316.56.
Total market volume was moderate at 225 million with 213 losers beating 152 gainers.

Most active was speculative Labroy Marine which rose to a new high of S$1.98 before closing at S$1.97, up four cents. A broker said there was no fresh news on the stock but several block trades were seen earlier in the day.
Engineering-based Van Der Horst recovered Thursday's losses to S$5.30, up 30-cents with 1.95 million traded.
DBS foreign ended 30 cents higher at S$18.30 and Fraser & Neave gained 20 cents to S$12.50 while Singapore Press foreign lost 50 cents to S$27.50.
